newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi delays lunch meeting with allies.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi delays lunch meeting with allies.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi has put off a meeting on Tuesday with party leaders in his centre-left coalition because of scheduling problems, his office said on Monday evening.
A spokesman said the meeting, scheduled to take place at 1300 GMT on Tuesday, had been delayed because a vote of confidence over the budget was expected at the same time in parliament.
He said the meeting, to discuss a planned mini-budget for 1997, would be held Thursday or Friday.

The spokesman said Prodi's meeting early on Tuesday with Fausto Bertinotti, leader of the hard-left Communist Refoundation party, was expected to go forward, as was his meeting at 1400 GMT with parliamentary leaders.
The time of the meeting with Bertinotti was not known.

Communist Refoundation is fiercely opposed to the mini-budget and a leader of the party was quoted in an interview on Monday as saying it might soon have to take difficult decisions over its support for the governement -- something Prodi relies on for a parliamentary majority.

Prodi is preparing a mini-budget in the next few weeks that could trim as much as 15 trillion lire ($9 billion) off this year's deficit to further Italy's chances of qualifying for membership of a European single currency at its start in 1999. ($1=1,656)
